newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - M.A.I.D sees profit early in 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - M.A.I.D sees profit early in 1997.

text.p: British online information provider M.A.I.D Plc expects to return to profit early in 1997, chief executive Dan Wagner said on Thursday.
"We expect to turn a profit early next year. We're not going to let the City down," Wagner said in a telephone interview.
M.A.I.D said its third quarter pre-tax loss narrowed to 2.4 million stg from 3.4 million a year earlier. It forecast a significantly improved performance in the last quarter of 1996.
Wagner said that M.A.I.D would unveil new products later this year but did not intend to take on Reuters Holdings Plc or Bloomberg in the provision of price-sensitive data.
Wagner said that new products were being developed for commercial release early in 1997 but he would not be drawn on exact details.
He said that M.A.I.D would not take on the likes of Reuters, Bloomberg and Dow Jones Telerate by seeking to supply real-time information to dealing rooms.
M.A.I.D supplies near real-time news, with stories reaching subscribers with a delay of a few minutes.
"We're on the desks of executives...It's there, outside the dealing room that we will look to dominate the sector," he said.
He said that M.A.I.D might steal some potential growth areas from other news services if it got a grip on the market it has selected.
The company has signed up 2,025 new corporate clients in the first nine months of this year. That compares with only 1,200 corporates recruited in the previous 12 years.

"These are quality clients who are paying many thousands of dollars per year to subscribe before usage revenues are taken into account," said Wagner, adding that the bulk of the new clients were in the United States.
